Implementation, tests, and docs for Story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md are present and aligned with the specification.
Key implementation: - Rule implementation: src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts - Header explicitly ties this rule to the story and its requirements: - `@story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md` - `@req REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING`, `REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT`, `REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX`, `REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT`, `REQ-VALID-OUTPUT`, `REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION`, `REQ-AUTO-FIX`. - Optional warning when @story + @req are detected (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING): - `analyzeComment()` computes `hasStory`, `hasReq`, `hasImplements`, `storyPaths`. - `processComment()`: - Early returns when `!hasStory || !hasReq` (no recommendation for pure @story / pure @req / pure @implements), matching backward compatibility intent. - When legacy pattern is present, calls `context.report({ messageId: "preferImplements", ... })`. - Auto-fix support (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT): - `buildImplementsAutoFix(context, comment, storyPaths)`: - Requires `storyPaths.size === 1`, exactly one `@story` line and at least one `@req` line, and a non-null `storyPath`: ```ts if (storyPaths.size !== 1) return null; const { storyLineIndices, reqLineIndices, reqIds, storyPath } = collectStoryAndReqMetadata(comment); if ( storyPaths.size !== 1 || storyLineIndices.length !== 1 || reqLineIndices.length < 1 || storyPath === null ) { return null; } ``` - Collects all `@req` IDs into `reqIds` and uses them in a single `@implements` line: ```ts const implAnnotation = `@implements ${storyPath} ${reqIds.join(" ")}`; ``` - `collectStoryAndReqMetadata()` only accepts simple, single-token `@story ` and `@req ` lines; any extra tokens cause it to bail out by nulling `storyPath`, so no fix is produced (REQ-VALID-OUTPUT, REQ-AUTO-FIX constraints). - `applyImplementsReplacement()` preserves order and structure (REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT): - Determines prefix from original `@story` line: ```ts const storyRawLine = rawLines[storyIdx]; const prefixMatch = storyRawLine.match(/^(\s*\*?\s*)/); const linePrefix = prefixMatch ? prefixMatch[1] : ""; const implementsLine = `${linePrefix}${implAnnotation}`; ``` - Rebuilds comment lines, replacing the original `@story` line with `@implements` and removing `@req` lines, leaving all other lines unchanged and in place: ```ts rawLines.forEach((line, index) => { if (index === storyIdx) { fixedLines.push(implementsLine); return; } if (allIndicesToRemove.has(index)) { return; } fixedLines.push(line); }); ``` - Reconstructs the full block comment, preserving the opening `/*` and closing `*/`: ```ts fixer.replaceTextRange( [comment.range[0], comment.range[1]], sourceCode.text.slice(comment.range[0], comment.range[0] + COMMENT_PREFIX_LENGTH) + fixedValue + "*/", ); ``` - `processComment()` wires fix into the report: ```ts const fix = buildImplementsAutoFix(context, comment, storyPaths); context.report({ node: comment as any, messageId: "preferImplements", fix: fix ?? undefined, }); ``` - Multi-story and mixed-annotation detection (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT): - `hasMultipleStories(storyPaths)` with `MULTI_STORY_THRESHOLD = 1`: ```ts return storyPaths.size > MULTI_STORY_THRESHOLD; ``` - In `processComment()`: - If `hasImplements` is true: reports `cannotAutoFix` with reason `"comment mixes @story/@req with existing @implements annotations"`. - If `hasMultipleStories(storyPaths)` is true: reports `multiStoryDetected` (no fix). - Configurable enforcement via standard ESLint severity (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY): - Rule `meta` has `schema: []` and no custom options; as a normal ESLint rule its severity is fully configurable (`"off" | "warn" | "error"`). - Plugin export in src/index.ts includes this rule in `RULE_NAMES` and maps `"traceability/prefer-implements-annotation"` to severity "warn" in the provided flat configs; the rule documentation shows how to set it to "off" or "error". - Backward compatibility (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION, Both Formats Valid AC): - Rule only reports when comments contain **both** `@story` and `@req`: ```ts if (!hasStory || !hasReq) { return; } ``` - Comments with only `@story`, only `@req`, or only `@implements` are ignored by this rule and remain governed by existing validation rules.

function onlyStory() {}`, ``` - Only @req is ignored. - Only @implements is ignored. - Invalid cases covering core behavior: - Optional warning & single-story auto-fix (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX): ```ts code: `/**

function autoFixMultiReq() {}`, output: `/**

 * @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED

function mixed() {}`, errors: [{ messageId: "cannotAutoFix", data: { reason: "comment mixes @story/@req with existing @implements annotations" } }], ``` - Multiple distinct @story paths trigger `multiStoryDetected` (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT): ```ts code: `/**
 * @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md

function multiStory() {}`, errors: [{ messageId: "multiStoryDetected" }], ``` - These tests validate detection, auto-fix behavior, multi-story/mixed cases, and backward-compatible ignoring of non-target patterns.
- Tests executed (via provided npm script): - `npm test -- --verbose --testPathPatterns tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts` - Command completed successfully (no error output), indicating the prefer-implements-annotation tests pass.
Documentation: - Rule documentation: docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md - Tied to the story and requirements at top: ```md @story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md @req REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING @req REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT @req REQ-AUTO-FIX @req REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX @req REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT @req REQ-VALID-OUTPUT @req REQ-BACKWARDS-COMP-VALIDATION ``` - Describes behavior matching the story: - Optional migration rule, disabled unless configured. - Explains that it detects legacy @story + @req blocks and recommends @implements with auto-fix where safe. - Documents limitations (no auto-fix for multi-story, mixed @implements, or unusual formats). - Includes concrete before/after auto-fix examples and explanation of message IDs (`preferImplements`, `cannotAutoFix`, `multiStoryDetected`). - Shows configuration with severity levels (off/warn/error) and makes clear that controlling behavior is done via severity (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY, Documentation AC): ```js rules: { // Default: off (no recommendations) "traceability/prefer-implements-annotation": "off", // ... or "warn" / "error" } ```
- User-facing docs: - README.md lists the rule under "Available Rules" with a short description and link to its dedicated documentation: ```md - `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation` Recommends migration from legacy `@story`/`@req` annotations to `@implements` (disabled by default). ([Documentation](docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md)) ``` - user-docs/migration-guide.md describes `@implements` usage and migration patterns (especially in section 3.1), consistent with the broader multi-story support and migration story.
Configuration & defaults: - The rule itself is implemented as a standard ESLint rule with no non-standard options (schema: []), so its severity can be configured as `"off"`, `"warn"`, or `"error"` like any other rule (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY). - The plugin’s README and rule docs show how to opt in to the rule and configure severity; by default (without configuring it in an ESLint config), ESLint keeps it disabled, which satisfies the "optional" and "backward compatible when disabled" aspects of the story.
Cross-rule validation: - Helpers for @implements validation live in src/rules/helpers/valid-implements-utils.ts and are used by the existing validation rule (valid-annotation-format). These helpers enforce: - Correct token count for @implements (MIN_IMPLEMENTS_TOKENS >= 2). - Valid story paths and requirement IDs via patterns. - Because prefer-implements-annotation rewrites legacy annotations into the simple, valid `@implements ` form and does not attempt fixes for complex cases, auto-fix output conforms to the validation logic in valid-annotation-format (REQ-VALID-OUTPUT).
Taken together, the rule implementation, its targeted tests, plugin wiring, and documentation demonstrate that all acceptance criteria and listed requirements for Story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS are implemented and passing.
traceability.notes: The project implements an ESLint rule `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation` that exactly matches the story’s intent: it is an optional migration rule which, when enabled, detects legacy `@story` + `@req` blocks, emits configurable recommendations, and offers conservative auto-fix support that rewrites eligible single-story cases into a single `@implements` line while preserving formatting. It also detects multi-story and mixed `@implements` patterns and reports them without attempting auto-fix. Comprehensive rule tests cover detection, auto-fix behavior (single and multiple requirements), non-fixable edge cases, and backward compatibility for comments that only use one annotation type. Dedicated documentation describes behavior, configuration (off/warn/error), and auto-fix examples. Existing validation helpers for `@implements` ensure that auto-fixed output conforms to the plugin’s validation rules. Based on the concrete code, tests, and docs, this story is fully implemented.
